title: The final product – your MSt dissertation
text: The final product – your MSt dissertation The basic structure: repeat the same ‘story’ four times 1. Abstract (An elevator pitch!) 2. Introduction (What motivates this research?) 3. Main body – literature review, analytical framework, data and methods, results and discussions (Can this study be replicated by following the descriptions in these sections?) 4. Conclusions (What’s the contribution? What should be done next?)

title: What is a literature review?
text: 1. What is a literature review? Lecture Plan - Is it just a log book of what you have read? - Is it just a part of your dissertation that nobody reads? 2. Why do we need a literature review? - Are there any guidelines and good examples? 3. How to conduct a literature review? - Pick a topic for your dissertation and let’s give it a go. 4. Practical session

title: What is a literature review?
text: What is a literature review? What are the most important and recent publications in a specific area (e.g., climate risks and commercial real estate valuation, discrimination against same-sex couples in the mortgage market, determinants of hotel vacancy rate, …)? Summary What has been done and are there any research gaps (What contribution can MY research make in light of the literature) ? Evaluation What methods and data should be used in MY research (e.g., quantitative vs qualitative methods, time series vs cross-sectional data)? Justification

title: Why do we need a literature review?
text: Why do we need a literature review? More often than not, we do not re-invent the wheels, but stand on a giant's shoulder. A good literature review helps us to find that “shoulder”. Evidence of knowledge and background One dissertation should answer one and only one question. What is your research question? Research focus Is your research novel and rigorous enough to meet the academic standard? Contributions

title: How to conduct a literature review?
text: How to conduct a literature review? There are some good databases and software packages Where to start? Check citation counts and journal reputation Who to cite? It depends! Clarity and coherence are important What structure? 20 – 40 academic publications, on average How many papers? The last 5 to 10 years are the most important. Don’t forget classics Time frame? Depending on the depth of the literature and the complexity of the research topic How long should it be?

title: Eexercise One – An Example
text: Eexercise One – An Example Instructions: Read the paragraphs on pages 2 to 5 and answer the following questions. 1. Can you find the full text of this paper, i.e., Gete, P., et al. (2024)? 2. Where can you find the cited papers online? 3. Can you tell the quality of the cited papers? 4. Are the cited papers relevant to the research topic? 5. What is the period covered by cited papers? Are they recent? 6. What purposes does the literature review serve? 7. Why did the authors cite Freddie Mac.(2021a and 2021b) in the Data section? 8. Why did the authors cite Abadie et al.(2022) and Bertrand et al. (2004) in the Specification section? 9. Why did the authors cite Rossi (2021) and Higgins et al.(2022) in the Results section? 10. Is the length of the literature review section appropriate for a MSt dissertation?

title: Eexercise Two – Create Your Own
text: Eexercise Two – Create Your Own Instructions: complete the tasks given below. 1. Download and install Endnote. Create a new Endnote file on your computer. 2. Open the Web of Science (WoS) database. Use the basic search to find Gete, P., et al. (2024). "Climate risk in mortgage markets: Evidence from Hurricanes Harvey and Irma." Real Estate Economics 52(3): 660-686. 3. Export the citation of this paper to your new Endnote file. Make sure you include abstracts in the export. 4. Download the pdf version of the paper from WoS, and add it to the Endnote entry. 5. Export papers cited by this paper to your new Endnote file. Make sure you include abstracts in the export. Create a Group called ‘Cited paper’ and put these papers in that group. 6. Go back to WoS search result page. Sort cited paper by Citations (highest first). Locate the most relevant paper (i.e., Do managers overreact to salient risks? Evidence from hurricane strikes, by Dessaint and Matray, 2017). Check the journal’s ranking. Is this a good journal?

Save the file in your computer. 11. Use Endnote to create a reference list for these paragraphs. Our article is novel in analyzing how hurricane-induced default risk translates into market- based mortgage pricing. Our results show that existing mortgage rates in the United States do not reflect the climate risks that markets would price. This result brings a different risk dimension to (Hurst et al., 2016), who show that lack of risk- based pricing provides insurance across locations. Another contribution of this article is to accurately estimate the increase in mortgage default probabilities caused by hurricanes. We show additional evidence of the effects of natural disasters on loan defaults (see, e.g., Kousky, Kunreuther, et al., 2020; Kousky, Palim, et al., 2020; Rossi, 2021). title: Eexercise Three – Shortcuts to the Shoulders
text: Eexercise Three – Shortcuts to the Shoulders Instructions: complete the tasks given below. 1. Go to WoS. Use the basic search function to find the following paper: Contat, J., et al. (2024). "When climate meets real estate: A survey of the literature." Real Estate Economics 52(3): 618-659. 2. Read Table 1 in Contat, J., et al. (2024). Do you think a similar table is helpful in your own literature review? How to create a similar table in Excel? Is it helpful for note-taking? Is meta-analysis or literature review papers good starting point for your own literature review? 3. Choose a topic that you are interested in. Pick four keywords to do a basic search. Note the number of papers returned from the search. Are all of them relevant? 4. Can you find literature review papers from the search result? 5. Save your search results. 6. Open one of the papers from the search result. Evaluate its relevance to your research topic.
